title: Odisha reels under incessant monsoon rains; major rivers in spate - News On AIR
article_text:
Odisha is confronting a grave flood emergency as incessant monsoon rains continue to swell major rivers across the State. The Baitarani has crossed the danger level, while the Mahanadi is also witnessing a steady rise, heightening concerns in vulnerable districts. The IMD has issued Red Alert for Sundargarh, Sambalpur, Bargarh and Jharsuguda districts and Orange Alert for thirteen others, with emergency response forces deployed in sensitive locations.

National Disaster Response Force teams have been deployed in the Red Alert districts to undertake rescue and emergency preparedness measures. The Salandi River has also crossed the danger level at Rajghat in Bhadrak district. As a precautionary measure, all schools in Bhadrak and Jajpur district will remain closed tomorrow, while rail services have been disrupted in certain stretches owing to waterlogging and adverse weather conditions. The State Government has assured that the situation is under constant surveillance and all necessary precautionary measures are in place.

title: Odisha reeling under heavy rainfall; fresh flooding in several districts - News On AIR
article_text:
Odisha is grappling with an intensifying monsoon crisis as a deep depression over the Bay of Bengal continues to bring heavy rainfall across the state. The India Meteorological Department has forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall till the 30th of this month in Mayurbhanj, Keonjhar, Balasore, Bhadrak, Jajpur, Deogarh, Angul, Dhenkanal, Subarnapur, Boudh, Nuapada and Balangir. Several districts have reported fresh flooding, waterlogging, crop damage and losses to infrastructure.

In Bhadrak district, the swelling Kansabansa and Gamei rivers have triggered a fresh flood situation in Basudevpur, where a second wave of floodwaters has inundated low-lying areas even before the first flood receded. Flood-like conditions continue in seven gram panchayats of the district, while extensive crop losses have been reported from Subarnapur. Rising waters of the Mahanadi have entered the historic Bhattarika Temple premises in Cuttack district. The State Government has strengthened preparedness and response measures, placing district administrations on round-the-clock alert to tackle the situation. Chairing a high-level review meeting, Revenue and Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari directed all district administrations to maintain round-the-clock vigilance and ensure swift relief and response measures as the State remains on heightened alert.

Woman killed in Idukki landslide as heavy rain batters Kerala

A woman was killed in an Idukki landslide as incessant rain triggered floods and fresh landslides across central Kerala. Rescue operations are underway in affected districts, while the IMD has issued red alerts for several districts forecasting extremely heavy rainfall.

BY PTI
PUBLISHED DATE - 1 AUGUST 2026, 08:45 AM

Idukki: A woman was killed after a landslide buried her house in the high-range Idukki district on Saturday, while incessant heavy rain triggered floods and fresh landslides across central Kerala, with several people feared trapped under debris in Kottayam district, officials said.

The deceased was identified as Sumathi, a resident of the Adoormala area. Debris from a landslide struck her house in the early hours of Saturday, the district administration said.

Neighbours managed to rescue her husband Ravi and the couple’s son. Both sustained injuries and were admitted to a hospital in Thodupuzha.

Authorities said the family’s house was destroyed in the landslide.

Sumathi’s body was recovered after a search operation carried out by personnel of the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), Fire and Rescue Services, police and revenue officials.

In another incident, a person was reportedly trapped after a landslide hit a house in the Vagamon area of Idukki district. Rescue operations were underway, officials said, adding that traffic in the area came to a standstill after debris blocked the road.

Meanwhile, at Upputhara, a parked police jeep was damaged in a landslide.

With the Pullakayar river overflowing, the Kokkayar low-level crossing (chappath) was submerged. Around six houses were inundated in the surrounding area, and the affected families were shifted to safer locations, officials said.

Authorities said several other landslides were reported from different parts of the district. Heavy rain also disrupted traffic at multiple locations.

The road between Kattappana and Vazhavara was blocked following a landslide, while rising water levels in the Chottupara stream at Vandiperiyar led to waterlogging on National Highway 183.

The road at Nellimala was also blocked, affecting vehicular movement.

Authorities have announced the opening of the shutters of minor dams in the district.

In the neighbouring Kottayam district, heavy rain triggered widespread flooding in Erattupetta, Kanjirappally, Koottickal and Erumeli, inundating residential areas, disrupting traffic and prompting large-scale rescue operations.

A house was buried under debris in a landslide at Payyanithottam in Poonjar, where two persons are feared trapped.

Search and rescue operations were continuing to trace them.

Erattupetta town witnessed a sudden rise in water levels overnight, forcing authorities to halt vehicular traffic.

Several houses in Erattupetta, including those in Nadakkal and Murikkoly, were inundated.

Rescue personnel, assisted by local residents, evacuated people stranded on the upper floors of their homes to safer locations. Traffic in the area remained completely disrupted, according to officials.

In Koottickal and Mundakkayam, water levels continued to rise after the Manimala and Pullakayar rivers overflowed. The Koottickal causeway and low-level crossing were submerged, while water entered several houses.

Traffic was also affected after the Mundakkayam causeway went under water.

More landslides were reported from the hilly areas of Pathanamthitta district.

Ranni MLA Pazhakulam Madhu, in a social media post, said heavy flooding had been reported in Ranni and adjoining areas. He urged people to remain cautious as river water levels had risen to dangerous levels and said floodwaters had entered several houses and shops.Legislative Branch

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast continued heavy rainfall in parts of Kerala, prompting authorities to keep rescue teams on alert and advise people in vulnerable areas to remain cautious.

The IMD issued a red alert predicting very heavy rain in Pathanamthitta, Kottayam, Idukki, Malappuram, Kozhikode, Wayanad, Kannur and Kasaragod districts.

An orange alert has been issued for Ernakulam, Thrissur and Palakkad districts.

District administrations announced holidays for schools in several districts in view of the forecast of heavy rain on Saturday.

title: IMD forecasts heavy to very heavy rainfall in Assam over next 3 | Akashvani News - News On AIR
article_text:
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall in parts of Assam over the next three to four days.

According to the IMD, heavy to very heavy rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms is likely from 30th July to 1st August across Assam, Nagaland and Arunachal Pradesh. The heavy rainfall in neighbouring Arunachal Pradesh and Nagaland is likely to impact the bordering districts of Dhemaji, Lakhimpur, Charaideo, Sivasagar, Jorhat and Golaghat in Assam. The weather office has warned that the intense rainfall may lead to waterlogging, flash floods, disruption of road traffic and localised landslides in vulnerable areas.

The Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA) said district administrations and emergency response agencies have been placed on alert and are closely monitoring the situation. The authority has advised people to avoid unnecessary travel during periods of heavy rain and to stay updated through official weather bulletins and advisories issued by local authorities.

title: Heavy rainfall continues to lash Kodagu; all schools shut - Deccan Herald
article_text:
A view of Triveni Sangama in Bhagmandala.
Madikeri: Heavy rainfall continued across the Kodagu district on Saturday, with Madikeri town witnessing incessant downpours since Friday night.
In Bhagamandala, relentless rain caused the water level at the Triveni Sangama to rise, inundating the park located along the riverbank. Floodwaters also entered nearby agricultural fields.
Following the heavy rainfall, district administration has declared a holiday for anganwadis, primary schools and high schools in Madikeri and Somwarpet taluks.

title: छत्तीसगढ़ में भारी बारिश से बाढ़ जैसे हालात, बीएसएफ के 30 जवान शिविर में फंसे, सुरक्षित रेस्क्यू - Arth Parkash
article_text:
Heavy rains in Chhattisgarh have led to flood-like conditions
जगदलपुर । Heavy rains in Chhattisgarh have led to flood-like conditions, छत्तीसगढ़ के बस्तर संभाग में लगातार बारिश की वजह से बाढ़ के हालात हैं। नारायणपुर जिले के अबूझमाड़ क्षेत्र में बारिश के चलते कुकुर नदी का जलस्तर अचानक बढ़ गया। इससे बालेबेड़ा स्थित सीमा सुरक्षा बल की 86वीं बटालियन के शिविर में बाढ़ जैसे हालात बन गए।
वहां तैनात 30 जवानों को जान बचाने के लिए आवासीय टिन शेड की छतों और पेड़ों का सहारा लेना पड़ा। बाढ़ का पानी कम होने के बाद समीपस्थ परयादी शिविर के जवानों ने बालेबेड़ा शिविर में फंसे सभी जवानों को सुरक्षित बाहर निकाला।
बस्तर में इंद्रावती नदी का जलस्तर घटने के बाद भी बीजापुर जिले से महाराष्ट्र और तेलंगाना को जोड़ने वाले प्रमुख मार्ग बंद हैं। कई गांवों का संपर्क अब भी टूटा हुआ है। भोपालपत्तनम के तिमेड़ पुल पर इंद्रावती नदी का जलस्तर 16.94 मीटर से घटकर 16.80 मीटर दर्ज किया गया है।
मध्य प्रदेश के खंडवा जिले में गुरुवार को तेज वर्षा के बीच हाडीकुंडी क्षेत्र में पिकनिक मनाने गए चार युवक जलस्तर बढ़ने से टापू पर फंस गए। करीब साढ़े दस घंटे चले रेस्क्यू आपरेशन में उन्हें सुरक्षित निकाला गया। इस दौरान टापू पर फंसे युवक तक भोजन, पेयजल व लाइफ जैकेट ड्रोन से पहुंचाए गए।
डिस्ट्रिक्ट कमांडेट होमगार्ड आशीष कुशवाहा ने बताया कि गुरुवार शाम पिकनिक मनाने गए खंडवा निवासी चार युवक टापू में फंस गए। तेज बहाव और रात के अंधेरे के कारण तत्काल रेस्क्यू संभव नहीं था। पूरी रात मोबाइल पर संपर्क बनाए रखकर उनका मनोबल बढ़ाया।
